q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. The NHS says you can give either paracetamol or ibuprofen if your child is distressed or uncomfortable, but check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable, or speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3]. Do not give ibuprofen to a child who is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [2]. Also keep giving plenty of fluids, and if your baby is breastfed, continue to breastfeed as normal [3]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
For vomiting, the most important thing is to keep your child hydrated by replacing the fluids they have lost [1]. Offer small sips of an oral rehydration solution often, rather than a large amount at once — you can buy these over the counter without a prescription [1][5]. If your child is on formula or solid foods, you can also give small sips of extra water [5]. Avoid fruit juice and fizzy drinks, as these can make vomiting worse [5].

If you are worried your child is becoming dehydrated, speak to a pharmacist, who may recommend an oral rehydration powder to mix with water [6].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration [3].

Offer liquids as oral rehydration solution. After your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [5]. Watch how well your child takes it; if the liquids are tolerated, you can slowly increase how often you give them [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids you can get over the counter are the most helpful for mild dehydration, according to the CDC [2].

Get help if your child is very dehydrated — severe dehydration may need fluids through a vein in hospital, so call your doctor [2]. The SEUP also says to see your pediatrician if your child is listless, vomits many times, or will not take liquids [3].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in young children, and croup is one cause: it often starts like a cold, with the cough and hoarseness worse at night, and most mild viral cases can be treated at home, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Asthma is another cause of coughing that is worse at night or early in the morning, according to the NHS [4].

Keep the room calm and comfortable, and offer fluids regularly. Do not put your child in a steamy room or have them inhale steam, according to the NHS [7].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if asthma treatment is not helping or the symptoms are waking them at night [4]. Ask for an urgent appointment if you think your child may have croup, or if they are getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [1]. Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the face, lips or fingernails turn very pale or blue [3].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last for 10 to 14 days [6]. If the cough comes in bouts and is worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound when gasping between coughs, it may be whooping cough [4].

Keep him comfortable and offer fluids often. If you think he may have croup — a barking cough like a seal, a hoarse voice, or a high-pitched rasping sound when breathing in — ask your doctor for an urgent appointment, because medicine may shorten the illness [3]. Also see your doctor if he is getting worse or not getting better [3].

Whooping cough can be serious, so it is worth checking: after about a week it causes coughing bouts lasting minutes, worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" or vomiting after coughing, and the cough can last several weeks or months [4].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with your child eating normally, is not one of the warning signs the NHS lists for a high temperature [1]. There is no need to treat a fever that is not there, and no medicine is needed for a cough on its own.

If a high temperature does appear, the NHS says not to undress or sponge your child to cool them, not to cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes, and not to give aspirin to a child under 16 [1]. Paracetamol should not be given to a child under 2 months, and ibuprofen should not be given to a child under 3 months, under 5 kg, with chickenpox, or who is dehydrated [1].

Get urgent help if your child is under 3 months with a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or higher, is 3 to 6 months with 39C (102.2 °F) or higher, has a rash along with a high temperature, has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more, does not want to eat or is not themselves, or is dehydrated [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly and itch can be hives (urticaria), which in childhood is most often caused by an infection, according to the SEUP [3]. The spots are raised, red patches that move around — appearing in one area as they fade from another — and hives can usually be treated at home [3][5].

If they itch, a pharmacist can advise on antihistamine medicine, and cooling creams or gels from a pharmacy can help [1]. Keep your child comfortable and don't let them scratch [1].

Get help urgently if there is swelling around your child's mouth or they are struggling to breathe, according to the NHS [5].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Your son has hit the back of his head, and the usual symptoms after a knock like this are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

Let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was — no sport and no screens during that time — then ease him back into his usual activities gradually [4]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He does not need any special food and can eat as his appetite dictates [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [6].

Watch for these signs at home: intense or worsening headache that does not ease with the usual medicine, repeated vomiting, disorientation or confusion, behaviour changes, difficulty speaking or walking, and blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [4]. Go to the emergency department if any of these appear, if his behaviour worries you, or if the fall was from more than one metre [5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, according to the NHS [2]. At first, how much they eat matters less than getting used to the idea of eating — they'll still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2].

Start with small amounts, just a few pieces or teaspoons of food, offered before a usual milk feed when your baby is not too tired or too hungry [5]. Offer a variety of foods: fruit and vegetables (including bitter ones like broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage), potatoes, bread, rice and pasta, beans and pulses, fish, eggs, meat, and pasteurised full-fat dairy such as plain yoghurt and cheese [1]. Include iron-rich foods like meat, fish, fortified cereals, dark green vegetables, beans and lentils [1]. Don't add salt or sugar to their food or cooking water [1]. Keep offering foods your baby rejects — it can take 10 tries or more [5]. Offer sips of water from an open cup with meals [5].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or first infant formula should still be their main drink, and you can offer sips of water with meals, according to the NHS [3]. Introduce a cup from around 6 months and offer sips of water with meals — an open cup or a free-flow cup without a valve helps them learn to sip and is better for their teeth [3]. Do not give whole cows', goats' or sheep's milk as a main drink until they are 1 year old [3]. During illness, increase fluid intake, including more frequent breastfeeding, and offer soft, favourite foods, according to the WHO [2].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula is no longer needed: once your child is 12 months old, formula milks are not needed, including first infant formula, follow-on formula, growing-up milks and other toddler milks [3]. Your child can now drink pasteurised whole or semi-skimmed cows' milk, and should be eating 3 meals a day with a variety of foods — starchy foods, fruit and vegetables, milk or dairy products, and protein — plus 2 healthy snacks in between [3]. Choose full-fat dairy such as cheese, yoghurt and fromage frais, because children under 2 need the vitamins and extra energy in them [3]. You can keep breastfeeding for as long as suits you both, but your child will need less milk to make room for more foods [3].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby: the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, and it is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is the consistency — constipation is stools that are too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, sometimes with fewer bowel movements than usual [6]. For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. If your baby is very drowsy and crying a lot, has blood in the stool, or vomits many times and cannot keep down solids or liquids, the SEUP says to have them checked in the emergency department [3].

For some babies aged 6 months to a year, night feeds may no longer be necessary, and some will sleep around 15 hours, most of it at night, according to the NHS [1]. Teething discomfort or hunger may wake some babies during the night [1].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on when a child lies down can be a sign of asthma, which often causes coughing at night or early in the morning [3]. Asthma makes the airways inflamed and narrowed, which can cause coughing, wheezing and chest tightness [4]. The main symptoms are problems with breathing such as wheezing, coughing, shortness of breath and chest tightness, and they may be worse at night and early in the morning [5].

Keep the room free of things that can trigger it, such as dust, mould, pollen or animals, and avoid cold air and tobacco smoke [5][6]. If your child has asthma symptoms, see your doctor [5].

Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the child turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [3].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
If your son needs his reliever inhaler more often than usual, that is a sign his asthma is not as well controlled as it should be, and he should be seen by his doctor [2]. Asthma cannot be cured, but with the right treatment most people can keep symptoms from getting in the way of daily life [1][2].

Keep giving the reliever inhaler as prescribed, and make sure it is used correctly — a doctor, nurse or pharmacist can show you how, and a spacer makes an aerosol inhaler easier to use and helps the medicine reach the lungs [1][3]. Do not change or add any other medicine on your own; the dose and type are the ones his doctor or the inhaler leaflet gives [3].

See your doctor if treatments are not helping, if he is needing his inhaler more often, if symptoms are stopping him doing his usual activities or waking him at night [2]. If he ever has an attack with severe difficulty breathing, that is an emergency — sit him up straight, keep him calm, and use the reliever inhaler as his action plan says while you get help [4].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the voice box and windpipe, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold and then causes hoarseness, a barking cough and high-pitched sounds when breathing; symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3]. Most viral croup is mild and can be treated at home, but if you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor right away [3].

Watch for difficulty breathing — breathing fast, the ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, or the belly moving a lot with each breath — and for a child who becomes floppy, sleepy or very irritable; if any of these appear, go to the emergency department [1][4].

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can have several causes, and one of them is asthma: chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply is a common symptom, often worse at night or during exercise, according to the WHO [1]. Symptoms like these can also be caused by other conditions, so it is worth talking to a healthcare provider [1].

What to do now: keep your child calm and let him rest; do not push him to take deep breaths or to run or play hard while it hurts. Offer fluids and watch his breathing.

Get help if his general condition gets worse — if he is listless, sleepy or very irritable — or if he develops difficulty breathing, such as breathing fast, the ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, or tiring when walking or running, according to the SEUP [2]. Chest pain when breathing is also a reason to be seen, the SEUP says [5].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A fever is very common in young children, and the temperature usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1]. A high temperature is 38C (100.4 °F) or more [1].

A febrile seizure can sometimes happen when a child has a high temperature [3]. If your child has another seizure, do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure [3]. Seek medical care if you think the baby is severely dehydrated [3], or if there is persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stools, or signs of dehydration [6].

After a period of rest, children usually recover quickly, within a couple of minutes [5].

If she starts to feel unwell again, she should sit or lie down straight away, and breathe slowly and deeply; the change of position is often enough [5]. If she faints, lay her down with her legs raised and her head to one side so she breathes more easily, and when the weakness has passed she can sit up slowly, then stand after a few minutes [5]. It helps children who tend to faint to drink more fluids, especially during exercise [4].

See a doctor if the faint happened during exercise or effort, or while she was sitting; if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the arms and legs, or if she wet herself at the end; or if she took more than 3 to 5 minutes to come round [6].

q: he has an inhaler but I dont know when to use it
text:
If your child is having an asthma attack, sit them up straight to help their breathing and try to stay calm, according to the NHS [2]. Use their reliever inhaler if they have one: with a blue reliever inhaler, give 1 puff every 30 to 60 seconds until they feel better, up to a maximum of 10 puffs, shaking the inhaler between each puff and using a spacer if you have one [2]. If it is an AIR or MART inhaler, give 1 puff every 1 to 3 minutes, up to a maximum of 6 puffs [2]. If their personal asthma action plan gives a different maximum, follow that plan [2].

Get medical help right away if they have severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turn very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Also get help if they start to feel worse at any time, do not feel better after the maximum dose, or do not have an inhaler [2]. If symptoms are no better after 10 minutes and help has not arrived, use the inhaler again, up to the same maximum dose [2]. Even after recovering from an attack, see your doctor within 2 days to discuss treatment and prevent another attack [2].

Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is constipation: fewer than three bowel movements a week, with stool that can be hard and dry and sometimes painful to pass, according to MedlinePlus [3]. A cough that is worse at night is common in several childhood illnesses, and the pattern of the cough helps tell them apart. In croup, a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing are usually worse at night and last about three to five days, according to the NHS [3]. Whooping cough starts like a cold, then brings coughing bouts that are worse at night and may end in a "whoop" or vomiting [4].

If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your health care provider right away [6]. Ask for an urgent appointment if you think your child may have croup, or if they are getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [3]. Get medical help right away for severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [5].

q: my 4 year old has earache after a cold
text:
An earache after a cold is often acute otitis media: infection and inflammation of the middle ear, behind the eardrum, which usually happens as a complication of an upper respiratory cold with a lot of nasal mucus, according to the SEUP [5]. It is one of the most common infections in children under 2 years old [5].

For the pain, the dose of paracetamol or ibuprofen depends on your child's weight; PediBot's dose calculator can work it out for you.

Get help if your child's general condition gets worse — if they are listless, drowsy or very irritable — or if they have trouble breathing [4].

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
text:
A blocked nose and trouble feeding are common in a cold: the usual symptoms include sneezing, a stuffy nose, runny nose, sore throat and cough, and they can last 10 to 14 days [2].

To help at home, according to the SEUP: keep the nose clear with nasal washes, and feed in small, frequent amounts to keep feeding and hydration good [1]. Hold your baby in a semi-upright position to make breathing easier, and keep them away from tobacco smoke [1]. Wash your hands often to avoid passing the virus on [1].

Get help if your baby breathes worse or faster, stops breathing for a few seconds or their lips change colour, has trouble feeding, refuses feeds or vomits, has fewer wet nappies with a dry mouth and tongue, is very floppy or fretful, or has a very high fever [7].

q: can I give Nurofen as well
text: No, do not give ibuprofen and paracetamol at the same time, according to the NHS [1]. You can alternate between them only if a doctor or nurse tells you to [1]. If a health professional advises this, write down when you gave each medicine so the doses are spaced evenly and you avoid giving too much [1]. Ibuprofen can be given 3 to 4 times in 24 hours, depending on your child's age and dose — check the packet or leaflet [1].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
A stomach ache with no appetite is common in children, and the NHS says it can be part of constipation — along with bloating or feeling sick — or of a stomach bug such as norovirus, which usually gets better in about 2 days [6][4].

For constipation, the NHS describes it as not having a poo at least 3 times in the last week, poo that is dry, hard or lumpy, or straining and pain when passing a poo [6]. If that fits, offer plenty of fluids and fibre-rich food, and speak to your doctor about a laxative if it continues.

If it is norovirus, the main symptoms start suddenly and include feeling sick, being sick and diarrhoea, sometimes with a high temperature, headache, tummy pain and body aches [4]. Keep offering fluids in small sips often.

See your doctor if the stomach ache is severe or keeps coming back, if your child is not drinking, or if they are not themselves.

q: my 8 month old hasnt had a wet nappy since this morning
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
A baby who has had no wet nappy since this morning may be getting dehydrated, and in infants this can become serious [2]. Keep offering small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution — the ready-made kind, not homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [1]. If you are breastfeeding, keep nursing normally, and more often if your baby wants it [8]. Do not give any medicine for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [1].

Get medical help right away if there is confusion, fainting, no urination, a rapid heartbeat or rapid breathing [2].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature can be looked after at home [1]. Keep breastfeeding as normal, offer plenty of fluids, and check on your baby regularly, including during the night [1].

Because your baby is 4 months old and has a temperature of 38C, get medical advice — the NHS says to seek urgent advice for a baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38C or higher, and for a baby of 3 to 6 months with a temperature of 39C or higher [7]. Also get help if your baby has a rash along with the fever, does not want to feed or is not their usual self, seems dehydrated (nappies not very wet, sunken eyes, no tears when crying), or the fever lasts 5 days or more [7].

Do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months or under 5kg, and do not give aspirin to children under 16 [7]. Paracetamol can be given if your baby is distressed, but check the leaflet or ask a pharmacist or doctor that it suits your baby [1].

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, fever after a vaccination is common and usually passes on its own.

The fever is often part of the body's normal response to the vaccine, and it usually settles within a day or two. Give plenty of fluids and let your child rest. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen if your child is uncomfortable, but the dose depends on your child's age and weight, so check the leaflet or ask your doctor or pharmacist. Do not give ibuprofen if your child has dengue, or purple or red spots that do not fade when pressed.

See a doctor if the fever is high, lasts more than a few days, or your child seems very unwell, drowsy, or is not drinking. The vaccination ages follow India's national schedule, so check with your doctor about which vaccines are due and when [3].

q: my son fell from bed and vomited twice
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
First, do what the warning above says.

A head injury with repeated vomiting needs to be checked, and the SEUP says to watch for repeated vomiting, intense or worsening headache, confusion or disorientation, unusual behaviour, trouble speaking or walking, and blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [1]. Keep him resting, both physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was, with no sport and no screens during that time [1]. If he is sleepy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine, that also needs attention [3]. Give fluids in small, frequent amounts, and if he is listless, vomiting a lot or not drinking, have him seen [5].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Most insect bites are harmless, though they sometimes cause discomfort, and mosquito bites usually itch [5]. The bite should get better in a few days [1].

To ease the itching and swelling, put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, or a clean cloth soaked in cold water, on the bites for at least 20 minutes, and keep the area raised if it is swollen [1]. You can use antihistamines to relieve the itching, or a hydrocortisone cream to reduce itching and swelling [1]. Do not let her scratch the bites, as they could get infected, and do not use home remedies such as bicarbonate of soda [7].

See a pharmacist if the skin around a bite feels hot or looks red, if it is painful, if the area looks swollen, or if there is pus or fluid coming out of it [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A cough that is worse at night can be a sign of asthma, which often starts in children and is usually worse at night and early in the morning [4]. It can also be croup, whose barking cough is often worse at night [5], or a cold-like illness such as RSV [2].

There is nothing in these sources about using a nebulizer for a 3-year-old who coughs at night, so I cannot advise on that.

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if asthma treatment is not helping, you need to use the inhaler more often, or symptoms are waking them at night [4]. Ask for an urgent appointment if you think your child may have croup, or if they are getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [5].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
A child who vomits everything and keeps nothing down has a general danger sign, according to the NHM, and needs to be seen [1]. While you get help, keep offering small sips of oral rehydration solution often, rather than a large amount at once [7]. If your child is breastfed, carry on breastfeeding and offer it more often than usual [7]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as these can make vomiting worse [7].

The SEUP says to go to the emergency department if a child vomits a lot and cannot tolerate solids or liquids, or vomits even without taking anything; if the vomit is greenish, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds; if the child is drowsy, listless, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or pees little; or if there is severe tummy pain or headache [4].

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर आंतों के संक्रमण का लक्षण है, और यह इलाज योग्य है [3][5]। घर पर सबसे ज़रूरी है शरीर में पानी और नमक की कमी न होने देना।

ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) का घोल पिलाइए — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का मिश्रण है, जो आंतों में सोखकर दस्त में खोया पानी और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट वापस भरता है [1]। साथ ही ज़िंक की सप्लीमेंट दीजिए: यह दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% कम करती है और मल की मात्रा में करीब 30% कमी से जुड़ी है [1]। WHO के अनुसार ज़िंक की 10–14 दिन की पूरक खुराक दस्त की अवधि घटाती है और नतीजे बेहतर करती है [3]। खाना खाने से रोकिए नहीं — दस्त के दौरान भी पोषक भोजन, जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है, देते रहिए; इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलिए, खासकर लंबे समय तक चलने वाले दस्त में, मल में खून हो तो, या पानी की कमी के लक्षण दिखें तो [1]।
sources: [1] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[3] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Overview", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/f

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दानों के कई कारण हो सकते हैं। NHS के अनुसार, हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह के छाले तथा हाथों-पैरों पर उभरे हुए दाने निकल आते हैं; ये लक्षण आमतौर पर हल्के होते हैं [3]। यह रोग आमतौर पर 7 से 10 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाता है और इसे ठीक करने के लिए कोई दवा नहीं है [1]। मुँह के छालों को आराम देने के लिए ठंडे तरल पदार्थ दें (खट्टे पेय, जैसे फलों का रस, न दें), दही जैसा मुलायम खाना दें, और गर्म, नमकीन व मसालेदार खाना न दें [1]। दर्द या बुखार के लिए पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है; खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है [1]।

अगर आपको लगे कि बच्चे को स्कारलेट फीवर या खसरा है, तो डॉक्टर से बात करें [1]। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद निकलते हैं — आमतौर पर बालों की रेखा पर चेहरे से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, बाज़ुओं, टाँगों और पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है [4]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में दूध कम पीना और पेशाब कम आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और जितना छोटा बच्चा हो, निर्जलीकरण का खतरा उतना ही अधिक होता है [1]।

अभी ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दें — घर का बना घोल या कोई भी कोल्ड ड्रिंक न दें [1]। स्तनपान कराने वाली माँ बच्चे को सामान्य रूप से, और माँगने पर उससे भी अधिक बार स्तनपान कराएँ [8]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ से पूछे न दें [1]।

SEUP के अनुसार, अगर बच्चा बहुत प्यासा लगे, बिना आँसू के रोए, पेशाब कम करे या आँखें धँसी दिखें, बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो, सुस्त हो या जवाब देने में कमी हो, दस्त इतने पतले और बार-बार हों कि बच्चा उतना पी न पाए जितना वह खो रहा है, खाना-पीना बिल्कुल मना कर दे, या पेट में लगातार या तेज़ दर्द हो या मल में बहुत खून आए, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

बच्चे को सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर ध्यान देना ज़रूरी है। SEUP के अनुसार, चोट लगने के बाद 24 से 48 घंटे तक शारीरिक और मानसिक आराम करना चाहिए, और इस दौरान खेल-कूद या इलेक्ट्रॉनिक उपकरण (टैबलेट, वीडियो गेम, स्मार्टफोन) का इस्तेमाल नहीं करना चाहिए [1]। इसके बाद धीरे-धीरे सामान्य गतिविधियों में लौटना चाहिए [1]।

मदद लेते समय, SEUP के अनुसार इन लक्षणों पर नज़र रखें: तेज़ या बढ़ता हुआ सिरदर्द जो सामान्य दवा (पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन) से ठीक न हो, बार-बार उल्टी होना, भ्रम या दिशा-भूलना, बहुत छोटे बच्चों में चिड़चिड़ापन या जगाने में कठिनाई, व्यवहार में बदलाव, बोलने या चलने में कठिनाई, और नाक या कान से खून या साफ तरल निकलना [1]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
बच्चे का बार-बार रोना कब्ज़ के कारण भी हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार रोने के आम कारणों में कब्ज़ भी शामिल है [2]। अगर बच्चा पॉटी करते समय तकलीफ़ में रोता है, तो यह उसी वजह से हो सकता है।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को शांत करने की कोशिश करें और रोना शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें — कभी-कभी इसके अलावा ज़्यादा कुछ नहीं किया जा सकता [1]। अगर आप समझ नहीं पा रहे कि क्या गड़बड़ है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर रोने के बीच बच्चा अपनी सामान्य हालत में वापस न आए, रोने के साथ पीलापन, पसीना, सुस्ती या दूध/खाना लेने से इनकार हो, या बच्चे को बुखार हो, उल्टी हो या पॉटी में खून आए — यह SEUP के अनुसार है [6]।
sources: [1] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/baby
[2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[6] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है, तो बच्चे को ठंड लगना, कंपकंपी आना और खासकर हाथों-पैरों की त्वचा का रंग जाल जैसा (cutis marmorata) होना सामान्य है, और जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना, लाल और गर्म हो जाता है [2]। बुखार शरीर का बचाव-तंत्र है, यह अपने आप में गंभीरता का मतलब नहीं है [4]।

बुखार में बच्चे को बहुत प्यास न लगे, थकान या सिरदर्द हो सकता है — यह भी सामान्य है [2]। बुखार का इलाज उसके कारण पर निर्भर करता है; अगर बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो तो डॉक्टर एसिटामिनोफेन या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी बिना पर्ची की दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं, और बच्चों को बुखार में एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। डिहाइड्रेशन से बचने के लिए पर्याप्त तरल पदार्थ पिलाना भी ज़रूरी है [1]।
sources: [1] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",
[4] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿QUÉ ES LA FIEBRE?", p. 1 —

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ज़्यादा देर जाग न पाना निमोनिया की गंभीरता के संकेतों में गिना जाता है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और उसकी साँस पर नज़र रखें — साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचना, सीने से कराहने जैसी आवाज़, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून व चेहरे पर नीली झलक दिखना गंभीरता के लक्षण हैं [2]। बच्चे को खाने-पीने के लिए मजबूर न करें, पर द्रव देते रहें [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बच्चे का कम पेशाब करना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और SEUP के अनुसार निर्जलीकरण का ख़तरा बच्चा जितना छोटा हो उतना ज़्यादा होता है [1]।

अभी सबसे ज़रूरी है निर्जलीकरण रोकना — ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) देना, जो तैयार मिलता है [1]। घरेलू घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक्स इस्तेमाल न करें [1]। घोल थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दें [1]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ से पूछे न दें [1]।

खाना बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं — बच्चा सामान्य खाना खाता रहे, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और ज़्यादा बार, बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करते हुए [8]। ज़्यादा चिकनाई वाले खाने, मिठाइयाँ और जूस से बचें; डेयरी उत्पाद ज़रूरी नहीं कि बंद करें, और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, माँगने पर और भी बार कराते रहें [8]। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक्स न दें — उनमें शक्कर बहुत ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [8]।

हाथ धोना बार-बार ज़रूरी है, बच्चे का और देखभाल करने वालों का भी, ताकि संक्रमण न फैले [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "Ofrecer en pe
[8] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार के साथ त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तो तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए — यह SEUP के मुताबिक आपात स्थिति का संकेत है [1]। ऐसे में बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों में न लपेटें और ठंडा करने के लिए पानी की स्पंजिंग न करें, क्योंकि बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। बुखार और दानों की स्थिति में बच्चे को डॉक्टर के पास ले जाएँ; दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है, इसलिए डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें [2]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS CONSULTAR EN
[2] NHS — "High temperature (fever) in children" (2025), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://w

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Paracetamol bukhar aur bechaini mein madad karta hai, aur aap ise 4 se 6 ghante ke antar par de sakte hain — din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ke liye sahi matra uske wazan par nirbhay karti hai, isliye dawa ki matra wazan ke hisaab se tay ki jaati hai [3]. Aap PediBot ke dose calculator ka istemal kar sakte hain, ya packet ya leaflet par likhi matra follow karein [3].

Agar bukhar se bacche ko takleef ho rahi hai to antitérmico dein, doctor ke aane ka intezaar na karein [3]. Pehle paracetamol se shuru karein [3]. Agar 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar tez hai aur takleef kam nahi hoti, to agle waqt ibuprofen dena theek ho sakta hai [5].
sources: [3] AEPap — "Antitérmicos (para la fiebre)", section "¿Cuándo utilizar los antitérmicos?",
[5] AEPap — "Antitérmicos (para la fiebre)", section "¿Cuándo utilizar los antitérmicos?",

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona bachchon mein aam hai, aur yeh asthma ka ek lakshan ho sakta hai [1]. Ghar par aap kuch cheezein kar sakte hain: bachche ko aaram karne dein, khoob saara tarral (liquid) pilayein, aur kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer istemal karein [6]. Khansi ke liye bina doctor ki salah ke koi bhi dawa na dein, khaaskar chhote bachchon ko [6].

Turant medical madad lein agar bachche ko saans lene mein sakht dikkat ho, tez saans chal rahi ho, ya chehra, hoth aur naakhun peele ya neele pad rahe hon [1]. Agar khansi ke saath bukhar 4 din se zyada rahe, ya lakshan 10 din mein behtar na hon, to apne doctor se milein [6].
sources: [1] MedlinePlus — "Asma en niños", section "¿Cuáles son los síntomas del asma en los niños
[6] MedlinePlus — "Resfrío", section "¿Cuáles son los tratamientos para el resfrío común?"

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli ke liye, yeh heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakta hai — yeh uncomfortable hota hai lekin aam taur par harmless hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6].

Abhi yeh karein: skin ko thanda rakhein taaki pasina na aaye aur rash na bade. Dheele cotton kapde pehnayein, halki bedding use karein, thande paani se nahiyein, aur paani zyada pilayein taaki dehydration na ho [6]. Khujli ya prickly feeling kam karne ke liye: thandi cheez jaise geele kapde ya ice pack (towel mein lipti hui) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur rash ko kharochne ke bajaye thap-thap karein [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Agar aapko yakeen nahi hai ki yeh heat rash hai, to doosre rashes ke baare mein dekhein [6].
sources: [6] NHS — "Heat rash (prickly heat)" (2024), section "Heat rash (prickly heat)", p. 1 — ht

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

Mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki — giri ke baad ulti hona aisa lakshan hai jise doctor ko turant dikhana chahiye, SEUP ke mutabik [1]. Ghar par is waqt dimaghi aur sharirik aaram zaroori hai, 24 se 48 ghante tak, chot ki gahraai ke hisaab se; is dauran khel-kood aur mobile, tablet ya video games bilkul nahi [1].

Dhyan rakhein: tez ya badhta sar dard jo aam dawa se bhi kam na ho, baar-baar ulti, bhram ya confusion, chhote bachchon mein chidchidapan ya neend se uthana mushkil, vyavhaar mein badlav, bolne ya chalne mein dikkat, aur naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aana [1].

Agar bachcha sust ya soya-soya lage, bahut pyaasa ho, aankhein dhansi lagein, aansu na aayein ya peshaab kam aaye, ya pet mein tez dard ho, to bhi turant dikhayein [3].
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO PUEDE V
[3] SEUP — "Vómitos. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿QUÉ SÍNTOMAS DEBEMOS VIGIL

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kuchh bachche kabz ke kaaran potty karte waqt rote hain — NHS ke mutabik kabz un aam kaaranon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bachcha rota hai [3]. Kabz aksar aisa hota hai jab bachche ka pet saaf na ho paaye, aur isse potty karte waqt takleef aur rona ho sakta hai.

Ghar par aap ye kar sakte hain: bachche ko aaram se pakde rakhein aur tasalli dein, kyunki kabhi kabhi rone ko shaant karne ke alawa zyada kuch karne ko nahi hota [1]. Agar aapko samajh na aaye ki kya takleef hai, to apne doctor se baat karein ya swasthya karyakarta se poochhein [3].

Turant madad lein agar bachche ko bukhar ho, doodh peene mein dilchaspi na ho, ya wo bechain ho aur shaant na ho [7].
sources: [1] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/baby
[3] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

Bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai — yeh ek aisi sthiti hai jismein turant madad lena zaroori hai [1]. SEUP ke mutabik, saans lene mein gambhir dikkat ke lakshan hain: pasliyan saaf dikhna, bahut tez saans lena, ya saans mein rukawat aana [1]. NHS ke mutabik, agar bachche ki saans lene mein dikkat ho — gurr ki awaaz, pet ka pasliyon ke neeche dhasna, ya tez saans — to turant madad lein [5].

Jab tak madad aa rahi hai, bachche ko aaram se rakhein aur unhe akela na chhodein [5]. Agar bachcha sust ho aur jagane par na jaage, to turant madad lein [5].
sources: [1] SEUP — "¿Debo acudir a urgencias? Guía rápida para padres y cuidadores" (2020), p. 1 —

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
Aapke bachche ki tez saans lena kai alag-alag bimariyon ka lakshan ho sakta hai, jaise bronchiolitis ya RSV, aur inmein shuruaati lakshan zukaam jaise hote hain jo kuch dino mein badh sakte hain [3][2]. Abhi sabse zaroori hai ki aap bachche ko aaram dein aur nazdeeki emergency department ya apne doctor se turant milne ki koshish karein.

NHS ke mutabik, agar bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai — jaise pet andar ki taraf khinch raha ho, seene ki pasliyan dikh rahi hon, ya saans tez chal rahi ho — to turant medical madad leni chahiye [3]. CDC batata hai ki RSV mein shuruaati lakshan zukaam, kam khaana-peena aur khaansi hote hain, jo aage chal kar wheezing ya saans ki dikkat mein badal sakte hain [2].

Raste mein bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, aur agar wo doodh ya paani le raha hai to thoda-thoda dete rahein. Agar bachcha sust ho jaye, uthne mein dikkat ho, ya honth neele ya grey dikhein, to ye gambhir lakshan hain — turant madad lein [3].
sources: [2] CDC — "RSV in Infants and Young Children", section "Did you know? Symptoms in infants
[3] NHS — "Bronchiolitis" (2026), section "Symptoms of bronchiolitis", p. 1 — https://www.

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night and stops a child sleeping is common with whooping cough, which starts like a cold and then brings coughing bouts that are worse at night [3]. The cough may last several weeks or months [3].

Keep the room cool and give small drinks often. Cough medicines will not stop the cough, and some should not be given to children under 12 years old [1].

See a doctor if the cough has lasted more than 3 weeks, or if your child is losing weight for no reason [1]. Get help urgently if the cough is very bad or quickly gets worse, if your child feels very unwell, has chest pain, swollen and painful glands in the neck, finds it hard to breathe, or is coughing up blood [1]. In babies, a pause in breathing or turning blue needs medical care right away [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash of small, raised bumps that feels rough, like sandpaper, could be scarlet fever, according to the NHS [5]. A spotty rash that appears on the head or neck and spreads to the rest of the body could be measles [5]. Spots that appear on a baby's upper body, scalp, cheeks, forehead and chin up to 6 weeks after birth could be baby acne, which does not need treatment and usually gets better after a few weeks or months [1].

Because your child is 5 years old, baby acne and nappy rash do not fit. Speak to your doctor if you think your child has scarlet fever or measles [5].

Get help now if your lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly become swollen, if you are breathing very fast or struggling to breathe, if your throat feels tight or you are struggling to swallow, if the skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale, if you suddenly become very confused, drowsy or dizzy, if someone faints and cannot be woken up, or if a child is limp, floppy or not responding like they normally do [7].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It's natural to worry when your child refuses to eat, and it's normal for young children to refuse food sometimes [5]. Don't worry about what your child eats in a day; it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week [5]. Keep offering a variety of foods and go back to foods they refused before — children's tastes change [5]. Give small portions, praise them for eating even a little, and don't force or reward with food [3]. Offer the same food as the rest of the family, with no added salt, and keep snacks to about 2 healthy ones a day [3].

Get medical help if your child is unwell and getting worse, is eating much less than normal, has had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more or shows other signs of dehydration, is very tired or irritable, or has difficulty breathing [6].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A congested chest with a whistling sound when breathing can be a sign of bronchiolitis, which often starts like a cold and then brings a cough, faster breathing and noisy breathing (wheezing), according to the NHS [2]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in 3 weeks [2].

Keep feeding your baby as normally as you can, and offer feeds more often in smaller amounts if they are finding it hard to feed [2]. Watch their nappies: a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or other signs of dehydration, needs medical help [2].

Get help today if your child is feeding much less than normal, has had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, is very tired or irritable, or if you are worried about them [2].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार आम बात है, और यह आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, भूख लगे तो खाना दें, और दिन-रात नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखती रहें [4]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [4]। 5 किलो वज़न वाले 6 महीने के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, क्योंकि यह 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चों के लिए मना है [2]। बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

डॉक्टर से सलाह लें अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा है, बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के और संकेत हैं, बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा से है, बच्चा खाना नहीं चाहता या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का नहीं लगता और आपको चिंता है, या निर्जलीकरण है — जैसे कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, और रोते समय आँसू न आना [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाएँ या स्पंज न करें — NHS के अनुसार बच्चे के कपड़े उतारकर या गीले स्पंज से ठंडा करने की कोशिश न करें, क्योंकि तेज़ तापमान संक्रमण के प्रति शरीर की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में भी न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार नापने के लिए डिजिटल थर्मामीटर बगल के ऊपरी हिस्से में रखें, बाँह को कोमलता से दबाकर शरीर के साथ टिकाएँ, और निर्देशों में लिखे समय तक रखे रहने दें [1]। अगर बच्चा अभी नहाया है या कंबल में लिपटा था, तो तापमान कुछ देर के लिए ज़्यादा दिख सकता है — कुछ मिनट रुककर फिर नापें [1]।

6 महीने के बच्चे को 3 महीने से कम उम्र, 5 किलो से कम वज़न, चिकनपॉक्स या निर्जलीकरण में इबुप्रोफेन न दें, और दमा हो तो डॉक्टर की सलाह के बिना न दें [7]। पैरासिटामोल और इबुप्रोफेन बारी-बारी न दें, जब तक डॉक्टर या नर्स न कहें [7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी जैसी आवाज़ होना श्वसन संक्रमण के कारण हो सकता है — SEUP के अनुसार प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ (सिबिलेंस) का मुख्य कारण वायरल श्वसन संक्रमण होता है [2]। ऐसे में बच्चे को आराम दें, तरल पदार्थ थोड़ा-थोड़ा करके पिलाते रहें, और उसे शांत रखें।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल, खुजली वाले छोटे दाने स्केबीज़ (खाज) के कारण हो सकते हैं — यह छोटे कीड़ों से होता है जो त्वचा में घुस जाते हैं, और उंगलियों के बीच पहले दिखने वाली उभरी लकीरें हो सकती हैं [4]। स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]।

इलाज शुरू करने के तुरंत बाद 5 साल या उससे बड़े बच्चे स्कूल जा सकते हैं, लेकिन पहले 24 घंटे दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें [1]। इलाज कीड़ों को जल्दी मार देता है, पर खुजली कुछ हफ़्तों तक बनी रह सकती है [1]। स्केबीज़ त्वचा के सीधे संपर्क से फैलता है, और यह सफ़ाई की कमी से नहीं होता [1]। खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण (जैसे इम्पेटिगो) हो सकता है [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो, त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे या एक्ज़िमा जैसी कोई और त्वचा की समस्या हो, कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों, या फ़ार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा करने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार, लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, जो मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, फिर भी ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का मामूली उपचार से इलाज किया जा सकता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना इसका संकेत है कि वैक्सीन अपना असर दिखा रही है [6]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi 3 saal ke bachche mein aam taur par asthma ke lakshanon mein shamil hoti hai: bachchon mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. Isi tarah, laringitis mein bhi bachche raat ko kaafi khansi karte hain aur theek se nahi sote [6].

Ghar par aaram karayein, khub taral (liquid) dein, saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein, aur saline nasal drops ya spray dein [4]. Khansi ya zukam ki dawa dene se pehle apne bachche ke doctor se baat karein, kyunki kuch dawaiyon mein aise ingredients hote hain jo bachchon ke liye recommended nahi hain [4]. Aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar saans lene mein problem ho ya saans tez chale, sharir mein paani ki kami ho, bukhar 4 din se zyada rahe, ya lakshan 10 din se zyada bina sudhaar ke rahein [4]. Asthma ke severe attack ke warning signs hain tez khansi, saans lene mein gambhir problem, aur chehre, honth ya naakhunon ka pale ya neela padna — aise lakshan hon to turant medical help lein [5].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko sir par chot lagi hai — SEUP ke mutabiq ise head injury (traumatismo craneal) kehte hain, jo aam taur par girne se hota hai [1]. Iske aam lakshan hain: sir dard, uljhan, thodi der ke liye yaad na rehna, chakkar, ji michalna, ulti aur neend aana [1].

Ghar par kya karein: baby ko 24 se 48 ghante aaram karne dein, jitna chot ki gahraai ke hisaab se zaroori ho; is dauran khel-kood aur mobile, tablet ya video games se door rakhein, phir dheere-dheere normal kaam par wapas laayein [2]. Agar sir dard ho to doctor ki batayi hui khurak mein ibuprofen ya paracetamol de sakte hain [6]. Baby so sakta hai, lekin zyada gehri chot mein use har 4 ghante jagana theek hai [6]. Khane mein koi khaas badlav zaroori nahi — apni bhookh ke hisaab se usual khana dein [6].

Turant madad lein agar: tez ya badhta sir dard jo aam dawa se theek na ho, baar-baar ulti, behoshi ya uljhan, bahut chidchidapan ya jagane par mushkil se uthna, baat ya chalne mein dikkat, naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aana [2]. Iske alawa agar baby 3 mahine se chhota ho, ya girne ki unchai 1 meter se zyada ho, to bhi turant emergency le jaayein [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) mein bhi sharir par dane aur kharish wali rashes ho jaati hain [1]. Sarna mein tez kharish hoti hai, khaas kar raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lines ban jaati hain; chhote bachchon mein hatheli, pair ke talwe aur sar ki twacha par bhi zyada gambhir rash ho sakti hai [1].

Agar aapko sarna ka shak hai, to bachche ko doctor dikhaiye — sarna ka ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai, aur yeh skin ke seedhe sampark se phailta hai, isliye ghar ke doosre logon ka bhi ilaaj zaroori ho sakta hai [4]. Doctor se poochhiye ki kaunsi cream ya dawa deni hai aur kitne din tak.

Turant madad lijiye agar rashes ke saath tez bukhar, saans lene mein dikkat, ya twacha par pus wale ghaav ya infection ke nishaan dikhein [1].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text: Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection of the gut, and the main danger is losing water and salts [6]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by 25% and cut stool volume by 30%, according to the WHO [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. See a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1]. The SEUP says to get help if the child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes; is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive; has stools so watery and frequent that they cannot drink fast enough; refuses to eat or drink; or has persistent or intense abdominal pain or stools with a lot of blood [3].

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Dizziness is one of the symptoms of heat exhaustion, according to the NHS [4]. Heat exhaustion usually does not need emergency medical help if you can cool down within 30 minutes [4].

Cool your child down and give them fluids [4]. Move them out of the sun and heat, and have them drink cold drinks [2]. Loose, light-coloured clothing helps, and keep them out of the sun between 11am and 3pm [2].

Get medical help right away if there is dizziness along with dry skin, a rapid strong pulse, nausea and confusion, which are signs of heat stroke, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Heatstroke is a medical emergency: get immediate medical help for a very high temperature, hot skin without sweating, fast breathing and a fast heartbeat, confusion and restlessness, seizure, or loss of consciousness [5]. While waiting for help, wrap them in a cool, wet sheet or sponge them down with cold water [6].

text: Give small sips of an oral rehydration solution often, to replace the water and salts lost in the loose stools — the WHO says diarrhoea should be treated with oral rehydration solution (ORS), a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar [1]. q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe, and it is not linked to autism: research has shown there is no link between the MMR vaccine and autism [4]. Protection starts within 2 weeks of having it, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps [1].

Common side effects are usually mild and only last 2 to 3 days, according to the NHS [4]. They include a raised, blotchy rash, feeling unwell and a high temperature around 7 to 11 days after the vaccination, and swollen glands around the cheeks, neck and jaw with aching joints around 2 to 3 weeks after it [4]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [4].

The ages at which the vaccine is offered follow India's national schedule.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text:
At around 6 months, you can start giving your baby solid foods alongside breast milk or first infant formula, according to the NHS [4]. How much they eat at first matters less than getting used to the idea of eating [4].

Offer a variety of foods, and let your baby set the pace. Some parents give finger foods and let the baby feed themselves, others use purées or a mix of both — there's no right or wrong way [1]. Your baby should be sitting safely upright in a high chair so they can swallow properly [5]. You can also offer sips of water with meals from around 6 months [5].

Keep breastfeeding or giving first infant formula until at least 1 year old; as your baby eats more solids, the amount of milk they want will decrease [3].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and it is often caused by constipation, which is usually harmless [2]. Constipation is likely if your child has not had a poo at least 3 times in the last week, or the poo is large, small, dry, hard or lumpy, or they strain or are in pain when they poo [1].

To help, give more fluids, preferably water, and more fibre: wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Do not replace fruit with juice, as juice has little fibre [3]. Keep to a regular routine and don't let them hold in the urge to go to the toilet [3]. Don't give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

See your doctor if the constipation comes with bad stomach pain, if your child is very down and complaining a lot, if there is blood in the poo, or if they vomit many times and can't keep down solids or liquids [3].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text: Malaria and teething are different things, and the early signs of malaria are easy to mistake for other illnesses. The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills, and the first symptoms may be mild and similar to many illnesses with fever, which makes malaria hard to recognise, according to the WHO [1]. Malaria is a life-threatening disease spread by the bite of certain mosquitoes, mostly in tropical countries, and it does not spread from person to person [1]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1]. If you think your child may have malaria, they need to be seen and tested by a doctor — malaria is preventable and curable, and treatment can stop mild cases from getting worse [1]. Severe signs include fatigue, confusion, seizures and difficulty breathing [1].

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text:
The main symptom of hives is an itchy rash, which can be raised bumps or patches in many shapes and sizes, appear anywhere on the body, and feel itchy, sting or burn, according to the NHS [3]. Hives rashes usually get better within a few days, and you can often treat them yourself [5].

Keep your child from scratching the bumps, because scratching can lead to infection [6]. A pharmacist can recommend treatments such as antihistamines and steroid creams [6].

See a pharmacist if the skin around a bump feels hot or looks red, it is painful, the area looks swollen, or there is pus or fluid coming out [6]. See a GP if a child under 1 year old has an insect bite or sting [6]. Ask for an urgent appointment or get help from your local emergency number if symptoms get worse or are not getting better, or if there is tummy pain with vomiting, dizziness or lightheadedness, a high temperature with swollen glands, or stinging in the mouth, throat or near the eyes [6].

q: my daughter has fever after coming back from a trip
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, a high temperature is very common and usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A high temperature is 38C or more; you can check it with a digital thermometer placed in the top of the armpit [1].

Fever is not an illness itself — it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are caused by infections, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Give plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration [3]. If the fever is very high, your health professional may recommend an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen; children with fever should not take aspirin [3]. The dose depends on your child's age and weight, so follow what your doctor or the leaflet gives.

Get help if your child is under 3 months old with a temperature of 38C or higher, is 3 to 6 months old with 39C or higher, has a rash or other signs of illness with the fever, has a fever lasting 5 days or more, is not eating or not themselves, or is dehydrated — such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [7]. Call your local emergency number if your child has a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it, is bothered by light, has a first fit, has unusually cold hands and feet, has changes to skin colour such as blue, grey, paler or blotchy skin, is drowsy and hard to wake, is extremely agitated or confused, has difficulty breathing, or is not responding like they normally do [7].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: At around 6 months, start with single vegetables and fruits, according to the NHS [1]. Try mashed or soft, cooked sticks of parsnip, broccoli, potato, yam, sweet potato, carrot, apple or pear, and include less sweet vegetables like broccoli, cauliflower and spinach so your baby gets used to a range of flavours [1]. Let any cooked food cool right down before offering it [1]. Foods containing allergens, such as peanuts, hens' eggs, gluten and fish, can be introduced from around 6 months, one at a time and in small amounts so you can spot any reaction [1]. Full-fat dairy like pasteurised cheese and plain yoghurt can also be given from around 6 months, choosing products with no added sugar [1]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [1]. The WHO adds that infants should also get animal source foods like meat, fish or eggs daily, and fruits and vegetables daily [4].

q: my 4 year old has severe cough and catarrh
text:
A severe cough with catarrh (runny nose) in a 4-year-old can be the early phase of whooping cough, which often starts like a cold with a runny nose, red watery eyes, sneezing and a mild or occasional cough, according to the Government of Canada [4]. This first phase usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks, and the cough then becomes more severe, with coughing fits that can make it hard to breathe [4].

Whooping cough is less severe in older children than in babies, but the coughing can still cause problems such as sore ribs, hernia or middle ear infections, according to the NHS [2]. Treatment depends on your child's age and how long they have had the infection; if whooping cough is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics are given to help stop it spreading to others, though they may not reduce the symptoms [6].

See your doctor so your child can be assessed and, if needed, treated.

A high temperature is very common in young children, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A fever is not a disease — it is usually a sign that the body is fighting an infection [2].

q: my 5 year old fell down and hurt his leg leg is swollen
text: For the first 2 to 3 days after a sprain or strain, follow the 5 steps known as PRICE therapy to help bring down swelling and support the injury, according to the NHS [2]. Protect the injury, for example with a support or shoes that support the foot or ankle; stop any exercise or activities and try not to put any weight on the injury; apply an ice pack (or a bag of frozen vegetables wrapped in a tea towel) to the injury for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours; wrap a bandage around the injury to support it during the day; and keep it raised on a pillow as much as possible [2]. To help prevent swelling, try to avoid heat (such as hot baths and heat packs), alcohol and massages for the first couple of days [2]. When your child can move the injured area without pain stopping them, try to keep it moving so the joint or muscle does not become stiff [2].

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
For a 3-year-old with watery stools and weakness, the main treatment is to replace the water and salts being lost. Give an oral rehydration salts (ORS) solution — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and continue nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode, according to the WHO [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by about 30% [1]. A 10–14 day course of dispersible zinc tablets shortens the diarrhoea and improves outcomes [3].

Contact a health professional if the diarrhoea is persistent, if there is blood in the stool, or if there are signs of dehydration [1]. For a child, warning signs to watch for include a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly or rectal pain, signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying, or stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus [2].

Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

q: my baby is not passing urine as much as usual
text: A baby passing less urine than usual can be a sign of dehydration, which means the body is losing more fluid than it takes in and can become serious if not treated [2]. In a baby, signs of dehydration may include fewer wet nappies than usual, a sunken soft spot on top of the head, sunken eyes, few or no tears when crying, and being drowsy or irritable [2]. q: how do I know if my child is dehydrated from diarrhoea
text:
A child with diarrhoea may be dehydrated if they are very thirsty, cry without tears, pass little urine, or have sunken eyes, according to the SEUP [2]. Marked irritability, drowsiness or a reduced response are also signs [2]. Other reasons to consult a health professional are diarrhoea that is persistent, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration, according to the WHO [1].

To prevent dehydration, give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the faeces [1]. Zinc supplements reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [2].

q: my 4 year old has cough with phlegm at night
text:
A cough with phlegm at night is one of the symptoms listed for pneumonia, which can range from mild to severe [1]. In whooping cough, coughing bouts are also worse at night, and a thick mucus can be brought up [3].

For a 4-year-old with a cough, the CDC advises: get plenty of rest, drink plenty of fluids, use a clean humidifier or cool mist vaporizer, and use saline nasal spray or drops [5]. Steam from a running shower can also help — sit with your child in a bathroom with the steam [5]. Honey can relieve a cough in children at least 1 year old [5]. Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines are not recommended for children younger than 6 years old [5]. For fever, young children can have acetaminophen or ibuprofen — contact your healthcare provider about the correct dose [5].

Get urgent help if your child has had a cough for up to 3 weeks, is coughing up yellow or green mucus, has chest pain that comes and goes or happens when breathing or coughing, or is feeling short of breath [2]. Call emergency services if your child is struggling to breathe, has pale, blue or blotchy skin, lips or tongue, is coughing up blood, or suddenly feels confused [2].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

The most common adjuvant, aluminium salts, has been used safely in routine infant vaccines for more than 70 years, and no harmful effects have been seen with vaccines containing it [1].

q: my 3 year old has severe chest congestion and flu
text:
A chest infection is an infection of the lungs or large airways, and it often follows a cold or flu [2]. The main symptoms are a chesty cough, sometimes with green or yellow mucus, wheezing and shortness of breath, chest pain, a high temperature, headache, aching muscles and tiredness [2]. These symptoms can be unpleasant, but they usually get better on their own in about 7 to 10 days, and the cough and mucus can last up to 3 weeks [2].

For the flu, rest and plenty of fluids help, and over-the-counter medication can reduce fever or aches [4]. Over-the-counter cough and flu medicine should not be given to children younger than 6 years old unless a health care provider advises it [4].

People with severe symptoms should seek medical care [3].

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text: It's a good idea to wait until around 6 months before introducing solid foods, and at the beginning how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to the idea of eating [2][3]. Start with a variety of foods — purées, mashed foods, cereals and soft finger foods are all fine, and there's no right or wrong way: some parents spoon-feed, some let the baby feed themselves, and many do a combination [1][2]. Your baby will still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula, so keep those going and let the amount of solid food build up gradually [3][4]. Offer sips of water with meals from a cup [5]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or GP when to start [3].

q: my 4 year old child has small red bumps on face and neck
text:
Small red bumps on the face and neck can be part of several common childhood illnesses, and what they look like and when they appear matters.

In measles, a rash usually begins as flat red spots at the hairline on the face, then spreads down to the neck, trunk, arms, legs and feet; small raised bumps may appear on top of the flat spots, and the fever may spike above 104°F when the rash comes out [3]. In roseola, the rash is made up of pinkish-red spots, patches or bumps, starts on the chest, tummy and back, then spreads to the face, neck and arms, is not usually itchy, and normally fades within 2 days [5]. Roseola usually causes a high temperature first, with cold-like symptoms, and children normally recover within a week [5].

If your child seems unwell, contact your doctor so the rash can be looked at.

q: my 1 year old baby body is very hot since morning
text:
A temperature of 38C or above is usually considered a fever in a baby, according to the NHS [2]. Feeling hotter than usual on the back or chest, sweaty or clammy skin, and flushed cheeks can all be signs of a high temperature [2]. Check it with a thermometer — that helps you work out whether you need medical advice [2].

You can usually look after your child at home when they have a high temperature: give plenty of drinks to avoid dehydration, and if you are breastfeeding, offer plenty of feeds [6].

Ask your doctor for an urgent appointment if your child has other signs of illness, such as a rash, along with the high temperature [6].

q: my baby has vomiting and loose motion since morning
text:
Vomiting and loose stools like this are often caused by a stomach bug, according to the NHS [1]. Gastroenteritis is usually not serious, but it can lead to dehydration, and babies are at higher risk [4].

Keep feeding your baby: continue breastfeeding normally, and offer it even more often if they want it [5]. Give small, frequent amounts rather than large ones, to reduce the chance of vomiting [5]. Oral rehydration solution is the main thing for replacing lost fluids [3]. Do not water down baby formula — use it at its usual strength — and do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, which can make diarrhoea worse [6]. Do not give medicine to stop diarrhoea to a child under 12 [6].

Contact a health care provider right away if your baby has a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, any fever in an infant, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe pain in the abdomen, or signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet nappies for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying [4]. Also get help if the vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [2].

While you get help, keep the child upright or semi-seated to make breathing easier, and keep offering small, frequent feeds, as the SEUP advises for bronchiolitis [6]. Watch the breathing, how well the child feeds, the colour and the general state [6]. If the child cannot feed or drink, or becomes unconscious, this is very serious, according to the WHO [7].

q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Yes, paracetamol (Calpol) can help if your child is distressed or uncomfortable because they have a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. It is a common painkiller for children that helps relieve pain and high temperature [4].

Give it at the dose recommended by your paediatrician, every 6 to 8 hours, according to the SEUP [2]. The main goal is your child's comfort — treat the discomfort, not the fever itself [2]. Make sure they drink plenty of liquids to stay hydrated, keep the room at a neutral temperature and ventilated, and avoid over-bundling them [2]. Do not bathe them in cold water or put wet cloths on them — it is unpleasant and does not work [2]. It is normal for them not to want to eat; do not force them [2].

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text:
Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts (ORS) to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS solution as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and ORS replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements as a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts and how much stool is passed [1].

Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

See a health professional, in particular for persistent diarrhoea, if there is blood in the stool, or if there are signs of dehydration [1]. The SEUP says to seek care if the child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes; is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive; has stools so watery, heavy and frequent that the child cannot drink as fast as they lose fluid; refuses to eat or drink; or has persistent or intense abdominal pain or stools with a lot of blood [3].

La urticaria también puede acompañarse, excepcionalmente, de dificultad para respirar o tragar [3].

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis es la inflamación de la capa externa del ojo y del interior del párpado, y puede causar hinchazón, picor, escozor, legañas y enrojecimiento, según MedlinePlus [4]. En la mayoría de los casos la infección se resuelve sin atención médica, aunque la conjuntivitis bacteriana necesita tratamiento con gotas o pomada de antibiótico [4].

Para las legañas pegadas al despertar, limpia los párpados con agua tibia; no hace falta que el niño falte a la escuela ni a la guardería, salvo que se encuentre muy mal [3].

Consulta a tu médico si tu bebé tiene los ojos rojos y pegajosos —con cita urgente si tiene menos de 30 días—, si llevas lentillas y tienes conjuntivitis con granitos en los párpados, o si los síntomas no se han resuelto en 7 días [3]. Pide cita urgente o ayuda si hay dolor en los ojos, sensibilidad a la luz, cambios en la visión como líneas onduladas o destellos, ojos muy rojos, o un bebé de menos de 30 días con ojos rojos y pegajosos [3].

text:
Las costillas que se marcan al respirar son un signo de dificultad respiratoria, y la SEUP indica que en ese caso hay que acudir a urgencias [1][5]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño incorporado y tranquilo, sin forzarlo a comer ni a beber, y vigila su color y su respiración [5].

Aunque después se ponga a jugar, el que se le marquen las costillas al respirar sigue siendo un motivo para consultar en urgencias, según la SEUP [1][5]. Si además tiene mal color, está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable, o rechaza persistentemente la alimentación y los líquidos, son señales de que hay que buscar atención de inmediato [5].

text:
Llamar a emergencias ya es lo correcto: no responde a estímulos y respira muy raro son dos señales de alarma que el SEUP incluye entre las que obligan a acudir de inmediato a urgencias [1].

Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén la calma y no lo dejes solo. Si vomita o tiene la boca con secreciones, ponlo de lado para que la vía respiratoria quede libre, sin meter nada en la boca. No le des nada de comer ni de beber, y no intentes despertarlo sacudiéndolo.

Si notas que se pone azul o grisáceo, que se le marcan las costillas o hace pausas al respirar, o que tiene movimientos anormales, son señales de gravedad que el SEUP recoge y que conviene decir al equipo que os atienda [1].
